description:
benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:487 sets:
  s.show_query_plans = s.capture_plans  # Show plans when capturing

This hardcodes show_query_plans to always equal capture_plans. The two concepts
are distinct: capture writes plans to the result bundle; display prints plans to
the console. After this assignment there is no way to enable one without the other.

Consequence in DuckDB: DuckDBAdapter.execute_query() calls
display_query_plan_if_enabled() at line 962 (guarded by show_query_plans) and
then capture_query_plan() at line 968 (guarded by capture_plans). Because
show_query_plans == capture_plans, when --capture-plans is active, both fire:
  1. display_query_plan_if_enabled() calls get_query_plan() → EXPLAIN ANALYZE (re-executes)
  2. capture_query_plan() calls get_query_plan() again → second EXPLAIN ANALYZE (re-executes)
For SELECT this doubles capture overhead. For DML (before the DML guard lands),
this causes triple execution: benchmark + display EXPLAIN + capture EXPLAIN.

The fix branch fix/duckdb-display-double-explain (commit 9fb1b334) guards the
display call with `if not self.capture_plans:` which prevents the double EXPLAIN
when capture is active. However, after this guard lands, display_query_plan_if_enabled
is unreachable in any configuration wired through `benchbox run`:
  - If capture_plans=True: the guard skips display
  - If capture_plans=False: show_query_plans is also False (from run.py:487)
  → display_query_plan_if_enabled never fires

The underlying issue is the coupling in run.py:487. Fixing it cleanly requires:
Option A (decouple): add a --show-plans CLI flag that sets show_query_plans
  independently. This restores the ability to display plans without capturing,
  useful for debugging single queries interactively.
Option B (simplify): remove show_query_plans as a concept entirely.
  display_query_plan_if_enabled() is only meaningful as an interactive debugging
  aid; promote it to a dedicated debug subcommand or remove it. The adapter
  constructor accepts show_query_plans from config but it is always False in
  production since run.py sets it to capture_plans.

Recommended: Option A. Restore --show-plans as a separate flag while keeping
the display-suppressed-during-capture guard from the fix branch. This gives
users a debug pathway without coupling it to result-bundle capture.

Note: this TODO depends on the fix branch (fix/duckdb-display-double-explain,
PR in progress) landing first, since that branch adds the correct guard. This
TODO then decouples the CLI flags cleanly on top of the guarded code.

anti_patterns.why: without the guard, enabling show_query_plans with capture_plans causes double EXPLAIN.

anti_patterns.why: that is separate from the display call and governed by show_query_plans for a different reason.

anti_patterns.dont: remove display_query_plan_if_enabled() from the base class
anti_patterns.why: it is called by adapters other than DuckDB and removing it breaks those call sites.

preserves.behavior: Adapters other than DuckDB that call display_query_plan_if_enabled() must remain unaffected.
Existing --capture-plans flag behavior (plans written to result bundle) must not change.
show_query_plans=True in adapter config (used by DuckDB PRAGMA enable_profiling) must continue to gate profiling.

Replace with:

This restores independent control. When --show-plans is passed without
--capture-plans, plans are displayed but not persisted. When --capture-plans
is passed, plans are captured silently (display suppressed by the guard in
duckdb.py, which is a prerequisite of this TODO).
